description: The failure classes an integration must tell apart, and what the daemon gives it to do so. `detected_by` says where the signal comes from: `transport` means no daemon answered, `http_status` and `tool_error` mean the daemon answered with an error body of the shape {error, code, help}, `job` means a job reached `failed` and carries `error`. An integration shows the user `help` when it has one.

classes.client_must: say that the daemon cannot be reached and how to start it; never invent memory content
say that a token is needed and relay `help`
treat it as the session's own choice, not as a fault, and say which operation was refused
report it as a bug in the integration or the model's payload, with `help`
report `Job.error`, and offer a retry through memcastle_job_retry
